questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: How many neutrons are in an atom of sodium-23 (atomic number 11)?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which particle carries a negative charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons carry a charge of −1. Protons, positrons and alpha particles are positive; neutrons are neutral.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the maximum number of electrons the n = 2 shell can hold?
questions.explanation: A shell holds 2n² electrons, so n = 2 holds 8 (2s² 2p⁶).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the ground-state electron configuration of Fe²⁺ (Fe, Z = 26)?
questions.explanation: Fe is [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². Transition metals lose the 4s electrons first, giving [Ar] 3d⁶.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which of these period 3 elements has the highest first ionisation energy?
questions.explanation: First ionisation energy rises across the period. P has the highest here; its half-filled 3p subshell is also extra stable.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: How many unpaired electrons does a ground-state chromium atom (Z = 24) have?
questions.explanation: Cr is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹: five unpaired 3d electrons plus one unpaired 4s electron = 6.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which of these isoelectronic species has the largest radius?
questions.explanation: All have 10 electrons. N³⁻ has the fewest protons (7), so the weakest pull on its electrons and the largest radius.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which set of quantum numbers (n, l, mₗ) is NOT allowed?
questions.explanation: l must be less than n. For n = 2, l can only be 0 or 1, so l = 2 is not allowed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which element has the highest second ionisation energy?
questions.explanation: Na⁺ has the neon configuration, so its second electron comes from a full inner shell close to the nucleus.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What type of bonding holds sodium chloride (NaCl) together?
questions.explanation: Na transfers an electron to Cl, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held by electrostatic attraction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: How many lone pairs are on the oxygen atom in a water molecule?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons: 2 are used in O–H bonds and 4 form two lone pairs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the shape of a carbon dioxide (CO₂) molecule?
questions.explanation: Carbon has two double-bond regions and no lone pairs, so they sit 180° apart.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the approximate H–N–H bond angle in ammonia (NH₃)?
questions.explanation: Four electron pairs give a tetrahedral arrangement; the lone pair repels more strongly, squeezing the angle to about 107°.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which of these molecules is polar?
questions.explanation: NH₃ is trigonal pyramidal, so its bond dipoles do not cancel. The others are symmetric and non-polar.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethene (C₂H₄)?
questions.explanation: Each carbon has three σ-bond regions (trigonal planar) and one π bond from an unhybridised p orbital: sp².

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the shape of a XeF₄ molecule?
questions.explanation: Xe has 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (octahedral arrangement). The lone pairs sit opposite each other, leaving a square plane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which of these has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: HF molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other, which outweigh the larger dispersion forces in HI.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the shape of a ClF₃ molecule?
questions.explanation: Cl has 3 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (trigonal bipyramidal arrangement). The lone pairs take equatorial positions, giving a T shape.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: At constant temperature, the pressure on a fixed amount of gas is doubled. What happens to its volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: pV is constant at fixed temperature, so doubling p halves V.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the molar volume of an ideal gas at 273 K and 1 atm?
questions.explanation: At 273 K and 1 atm one mole of ideal gas occupies 22.4 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: The SI unit is the pascal: 1 Pa = 1 N m⁻².

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: A gas at 300 K is heated to 600 K at constant pressure. What happens to its volume?
questions.explanation: Charles's law: V/T is constant at fixed pressure. Doubling the kelvin temperature doubles V.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: At the same temperature, which gas diffuses fastest?
questions.explanation: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M. H₂ has the lowest molar mass (2 g mol⁻¹).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: How many moles are in 4.0 g of helium (He = 4.0)?
questions.explanation: n = m / M = 4.0 g ÷ 4.0 g mol⁻¹ = 1.0 mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the ratio of the effusion rates of H₂ to O₂ at the same temperature?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Under which conditions does a real gas deviate most from ideal behaviour?
questions.explanation: At high pressure molecular volume matters, and at low temperature intermolecular attractions matter.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: A mixture of 2 mol N₂ and 3 mol O₂ has a total pressure of 100 kPa. What is the partial pressure of N₂?
questions.explanation: Dalton's law: p(N₂) = mole fraction × total = (2/5) × 100 kPa = 40 kPa.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of:
questions.explanation: Atomic number (Z) is the number of protons. Protons plus neutrons is the mass number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Isotopes of an element have the same number of:
questions.explanation: Isotopes share the same atomic number (protons) but have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: By the Aufbau principle, which subshell fills immediately after 4s?
questions.explanation: The filling order is … 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p …, so 3d fills after 4s.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: How many orbitals are in a d subshell?
questions.explanation: For l = 2, mₗ runs from −2 to +2: five orbitals, holding up to 10 electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which ion has the same electron configuration as argon?
questions.explanation: K⁺ has 19 − 1 = 18 electrons, like Ar. Ca⁺ has 19; Na⁺, Al³⁺ and Mg²⁺ have 10 (neon).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Why is the first ionisation energy of oxygen lower than that of nitrogen?

options.text: Oxygen removes an electron from a paired 2p orbital, where repulsion makes it easier to remove
Oxygen has a smaller nuclear charge
Oxygen's outer electron is in a higher shell

questions.explanation: O is 2p⁴: one 2p orbital holds a pair, and electron–electron repulsion makes that electron easier to remove. N's half-filled 2p³ is more stable.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which molecule contains a triple bond?
questions.explanation: Each N needs three more electrons, so N₂ shares three pairs: N≡N.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What type of bond forms when two atoms share a pair of electrons?
questions.explanation: A shared electron pair is a covalent bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the shape of a BF₃ molecule?
questions.explanation: B has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so they spread to 120° in a plane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which species contains a dative covalent bond?
questions.explanation: In NH₄⁺ the N lone pair is donated to H⁺, forming a dative (coordinate) bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is the shape of an SF₄ molecule?
questions.explanation: S has 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair (trigonal bipyramidal arrangement). The lone pair sits equatorial, giving a see-saw.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: How many σ and π bonds are in ethyne (C₂H₂)?
questions.explanation: H–C≡C–H: two C–H σ bonds, and the triple bond is one σ plus two π.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is absolute zero on the Celsius scale (to the nearest degree)?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Which is the ideal gas equation?
questions.explanation: pV = nRT, with p in Pa, V in m³, n in mol and T in K.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What is 27 °C in kelvin?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: What volume does 0.5 mol of an ideal gas occupy at 273 K and 1 atm?
questions.explanation: 0.5 mol × 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹ = 11.2 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: 1.0 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K occupies 8.314 dm³. What is its pressure? (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: At room temperature and pressure, which gas behaves most like an ideal gas?
questions.explanation: He atoms are tiny with only weak dispersion forces. NH₃, H₂O and HCl are polar, and CO₂ has stronger dispersion forces.
